overview: Spicy's Sprint is an always-sprint override that re-asserts sprinting on every pre-tick. On EventUpdate pre, if the player is pushing forward (moveForward > 0) and not using an item, not sneaking and not collided horizontally, it calls setSprinting(true) and zeroes arrowHitTimer. It deliberately drops the vanilla gates: the food-level check (vanilla requires foodLevel above 6 or flight), the double-tap and sprint-key requirements, and the post-hit timer. Because the fork's setSprinting sends no packet and onUpdateWalkingPlayer emits the C0B entity-action only on sprint-state transitions, the wire effect is one C0B START_SPRINTING on the first tick and an ordinary sprint-speed C03 stream afterwards; onDisable restores the honest state (sprint only if the key is held), which emits STOP when the key is not down.

sections.p: The module's condition is a subset of vanilla's. Vanilla additionally demands foodLevel > 6 (or allowFlying), the sprint key or the double-tap toggle timer, and no arrow-hit state; the module keeps only the movement-side gates. Because the EventUpdate pre dispatch runs at the top of onUpdateWalkingPlayer, before the C0B dedup, the forced setSprinting(true) is what the dedup reads: flag = isSprinting() != serverSprintState, so exactly one START_SPRINTING goes out on the first tick and, since the module re-asserts sprint before every subsequent comparison, no STOP is ever emitted while it runs. The arrowHitTimer = 0 line is a template leftover: in this fork the field is only touched by the server-side arrow-count logic in EntityLivingBase.onUpdate (the !worldObj.isRemote branch), so on the client it is inert.

Sprinting is client-declared: the server learns it only from the C0B, which the module sends legitimately, and the C03 stream at sprint speed is inside every legal envelope. The residual differences are the ones the module chooses not to model: sprinting while starving (vanilla stops at foodLevel 6 and below, and NCP flags 5 and below), and sprinting without any key or double-tap gesture. Everything else — speed, direction, packet rate — is ordinary sprinting, which is why the module's detection story is mostly about the gates it omits rather than the speed it produces.

files.label: Sprint.java (module)
files.explanation:
The module is one pre-update branch plus a restore. The condition requires forward input and excludes item use, sneaking and horizontal collision — the movement-side vanilla gates — but omits the food gate, the key/toggle requirement and the post-hit state, which is the whole point of an always-sprint module: it sprints in states where vanilla would refuse.

onDisable is the module's honesty contract: it calls setSprinting(gameSettings.keyBindSprint.isKeyDown()), so the player's sprint state snaps back to the key binding the moment the module turns off, and the C0B dedup in onUpdateWalkingPlayer emits the matching STOP when the key is not held. The two-line lifecycle — force on, restore on disable — is the entire module.

files.label: EntityPlayerSP.java (sprint gates and C0B emission)
files.explanation:
Two regions matter. onUpdateWalkingPlayer (lines 225-237) is where the module's flag becomes wire traffic: flag = isSprinting(); if flag != serverSprintState, send C0B START/STOP and latch the state — so the module's per-tick setSprinting(true) collapses to a single START, and re-assertion before the comparison is what prevents STOP from ever being sent mid-run.

onLivingUpdate (lines 846-868) holds the vanilla gates the module skips: flag3 = foodLevel > 6 || allowFlying, the double-tap sprintToggleTimer path, the key-hold sprint, and the stop condition (moveForward < 0.8, horizontal collision, or food). Comparing the two regions shows exactly which gates the module bypasses and which it inherits: it can sprint while starving and without any gesture, but it still refuses to sprint while using an item, sneaking, or touching a wall.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (illegal-sprint branch)
countering.explanation:
Beyond the speed envelope, SurvivalFly carries an illegal-sprint branch at the top of its horizontal prediction (line 877): when the server's sprint flag is set and the WASD input model is known, it flags sprinting whose input is not purely forward — forwardDir != FORWARD with strafe input — or whose food level is 5 or below, tagging the move 'illegalsprint', feeding Improbable with 'moving.survivalfly.illegalsprint', resetting the horizontal data and returning a violation.

The food half is the direct counter to this module: Spicy Sprint never checks hunger, so a starving user keeps sprinting while vanilla would have stopped at foodLevel 6 and NCP punishes at 5 and below. The input half does not apply — the module only sprints with moveForward > 0 — which is the precise boundary the branch draws: sprinting while moving forward is legal, sprinting in states vanilla forbids is not.

countering.label: SprintDirection (sprint movement angle)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's SprintDirection verifies that a sprinting player's movement actually points where they look: it reconstructs the move force from the delta and the previous velocity, divides by friction, adds the 0.2 sprint-jump push when the move is a jump, and punishes when the angle between the move vector and the yaw exceeds PI/4 + 0.3 (about 75 degrees). It exempts knockback-accepted moves, teleports, ladders, vines and the first two ticks after a sprint start.

The module's moveForward > 0 guard guarantees forward motion, so the movement vector always stays within the angle window and the check passes. It is the boundary for the omni-sprint family — modules that sprint while strafing or walking backwards produce exactly the angle mismatch this check punishes — and Spicy Sprint deliberately avoids that family by gating on forward input.

countering.label: Speed (ground-move expectation)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Speed compares per-move horizontal distance against an expectation built from getBaseMoveSpeed, a 0.2873 walking/sprinting base scaled by speed-potion amplifiers, plus stage constants for jumps and special surfaces. A grounded sprint move measures about 0.286 per tick against that 0.2873 expectation, and the on-ground branch only flags when thisMove exceeds the expected velocity with at least five grounded ticks of history.

The module adds no horizontal gain beyond vanilla sprint speed — it only changes when sprinting is allowed, not how fast sprinting moves — so every C03 lands inside the expectation and the check passes. The entry documents the boundary: sprint state itself is not a violation surface in Arc; only the speed that state produces is, and this module produces exactly the legal amount.
